claims.text: The deviation is established on the governing measurement. EV-GPS-09113 records trace_distance_km of 18.0 km between the recorded pickup and dropoff, and EV-TRIP-09113 records the booking-time optimal at 10.0 km, so the excess is 8.0 km — 80% of optimal. Both POL-RD-01 tests are passed (more than 20% and more than 0.8 km), and 80% also exceeds the 50% materiality gate. POL-RD-01 makes the trace figure governing over the rounded trip_record.actual_distance_km, so the threshold rests on the authoritative measurement, not the convenience copy.

The rider accepts the closure and the detour it forced — but the closure only explains part of the detour. Under POL-RD-03 the exonerated excess is capped at the lesser of the measured 8.0 km or 1.30 x (shortest_lawful_alternative_km 12.0 - optimal 10.0) + 1.00 km = 3.6 km. EV-ADVIS-09113-01 therefore justifies 3.6 km of the excess and no more. The remaining 4.4 km — 44% of the booked optimal, well past the POL-RD-01 threshold — is unexplained by the advisory and remains an unexcused deviation. The rider's acceptance of the closure in chat is not a waiver of the excess beyond what the closure required.

The refund is arithmetic under POL-RD-02, run against the closure-adjusted optimal. Adjusted optimal distance = 10.0 + 3.6 = 13.6 km; adjusted duration = 20.0 min scaled by 13.6/10.0 = 27.2 min (trip_record.amended_optimal_duration_min is null, so the scaled figure governs). Recomputed fare = (3.80 + 0.75 x 13.6 + 0.28 x 27.2) x the surge_multiplier of 1.00 read from EV-FARE-09113, plus the 0.80 platform fee, plus the 1.00 of on-optimal-route ERP, plus a waiting_time_fee of 0.00, less a promo_discount of 0.00 = 23.416. Charged_total is 31.42. Refund = 31.42 - 23.416 = 8.004, rounded up to SGD 8.05 — not de minimis, and 25.6% of charged_total so it does not convert to a full refund.

The driver's only candidate excuse, a rider-requested detour, cannot run. The single rider message in the chat log, MSG-09113-002 at 18:23:10, reads 'Understood, please take the lawful diversion'. It names no road and no place, and its waypoint_hint is null, so it is not an instruction 'specific enough to act on' and the 200 m corroboration test cannot be performed on the record. Under POL-RD-04 the clause is unavailable and the case is decided on the remaining clauses; the message that does name a road (Pelton Canal Link) is the driver's own, and a driver's own message cannot be a rider instruction.

No impairment discount touches the measurement the rider relies on. EV-GPS-09113 carries 205 fixes at a 10-second sample interval, 100% coverage, zero gaps and a max_gap_sec of 0.0, and its admissibility status is COMPLETE at weight_multiplier 1.0. None of POL-RD-07 limbs (a) to (c) fires, so no independent corroboration is required for the excess and no confidence cap arises under POL-GEN-02 in respect of this artifact.

The off-route ERP is recovered once and not twice. EV-FARE-09113 marks the 'Industrial loop exit' gantry (2.80) as on_optimal_route false and only the 1.00 'Pelton lawful diversion entry' gantry as on the optimal route; because the recomputed fare above already excludes the 2.80 line, POL-RD-09(1) means that off-route ERP is comprehended inside the POL-RD-02 refund and must never be added on top of it. The rider claims that 2.80 only through the recomputation, and the ruling should itemise it for transparency without double-counting it.

The rider's initial burden under POL-RD-08 is discharged on the face of the record: trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown all carry trip_id TRP-09113 with a consistent 18:20 pickup start, and limb (b) is met by a 4.4 km residual excess (44% of the adjusted optimal) measured from an unimpaired trace. The burden has shifted to the driver, and the only clause he points to, POL-RD-04, is unavailable on the chat log — a general assertion that 'the closure forced a diversion' is answered by the POL-RD-03 cap itself, not by any further evidence he has produced.

No elevated corroboration requirement applies to this rider. EV-RPROF-09113 records deviation_claims_60d of 0 and deviation_claims_60d_substantiated of 0, far below the 4-or-more trigger in POL-RD-08, so the excess need not be corroborated beyond the gps_trace. This is the only use the rider's profile is put to, and POL-GEN-01 confines it to that test; the rider's other profile counters are not relied on for any finding.

claims.text: The LTA advisory on this trip — ADV-20260920-113, severity HIGH, type CLOSURE, road 'Pelton Canal Link eastbound connector', shortest lawful alternative 12.0 km — is precisely the event POL-RD-03 exonerates. Limb (a): it names a road the optimal route traverses, and the trip record's own optimal route source says the estimate ran 'via Pelton Canal Link, the segment named in the LTA advisory'. Limb (b): its validity window of 18:14 to 18:55 brackets the whole driving window shown by the trace (first fix 18:20:00, last fix 18:54:00) with far more than the 15-minute buffer at each end. Limb (c): the fare breakdown places the vehicle on the 'Industrial loop exit' gantry at lat 1.338, lng 103.897 — inside the advisory's own geometry bounds of lat 1.320–1.341, lng 103.871–103.899 — and that gantry is flagged on_optimal_route false, so the actual route left the optimal corridor at the closed segment and rejoined it after. The closure exoneration is engaged and must be applied before any refund is computed.

The exoneration is capped, and the cap is arithmetic that the record supplies in full: justified_excess = min(measured_excess, 1.30 x (shortest_lawful_alternative_km - optimal_distance_km) + 1.00) = min(8.0, 1.30 x (12.0 - 10.0) + 1.00) = min(8.0, 3.60) = 3.60 km. The 8.0 km of excess on the trace is therefore exonerated only as to 3.6 km. The closure-adjusted optimal is 10.0 + 3.6 = 13.6 km, and its duration is the booked 20.0 minutes scaled by 13.6/10.0, i.e. 27.2 minutes, because the trip record stores no amended optimal duration. Only the remaining 4.4 km may be charged against the driver at all.

Because POL-RD-02 must run against the closure-adjusted optimal and not the booked one, the driver's maximum exposure is the recomputed fare: (3.80 + 0.75 x 13.6 + 0.28 x 27.2) x 1.0 surge — the multiplier read from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier, the only artifact that carries the field — plus 0.80 platform fee plus 1.00 of ERP for the single gantry lying on the optimal route, which is 23.416, against a charged_total of 31.42. That caps the distance-and-time refund at 8.004, rounded up to 8.05. The same arithmetic run against the unadjusted optimal would produce 12.72; the 3.60 km of closure exoneration is worth 4.67 to the driver and is not available to be refunded. No figure above 8.05 can be reached on this record.

The material deviation requires the POL-RD-06 driver_profile check, and the check comes back clean. driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 and driver_profile.completed_trips_90d is 610, a ratio of 0.000 against the 0.05 the clause demands, and the absolute counter of 3 flags is not met either. No repeat pattern is established, so POL-RD-06(b)'s FULL_REFUND uplift of the whole charged_total is not available to the rider, and POL-RD-06(c)'s driver-conduct referral is not triggered. POL-GEN-01 confines this check to those two named fields: driver_profile.prior_deviation_flags (0) is a lifetime counter and is not the trailing-90-day field POL-RD-06 names, and the rest of the profile — rating 4.89, acceptance rate 0.94, lifetime trips 2140 — is context only and may not ground any finding.

The 2.80 'Industrial loop exit' gantry is off the optimal route, and the rider is already made whole for it inside the POL-RD-02 refund, which is charged_total less a recomputed fare built only from gantries lying on the optimal route. Under POL-RD-09(1) that line is comprehended in the refund and must never be added on top of it. POL-RD-09(2)'s standalone pass-through correction is not the right limb here: that limb applies where the deviation is exonerated as an external event, whereas here the exoneration is partial, POL-RD-02 runs on the closure-adjusted optimal and limb (1) governs. Refunding the ERP a second time would take the rider past 8.05 for a cost the distance refund has already returned.

The governing distance is the trace, and the trace is clean: gps_trace.trace_distance_km is 18.0 km over 205 fixes at a 10-second sample interval, coverage 100%, no gaps recorded and max_gap_sec 0.0, admissibility COMPLETE at weight 1.0. The trace therefore does not meet any limb of POL-RD-07(a) to (c) and is not impaired for policy purposes: no straight-line substitution is available, no independent corroboration is required, and no escalation under POL-RD-10(3) is open on this record. The excess is measured once, at 8.0 km, on an unimpaired trace, and trip_record.actual_distance_km may not be cited for the threshold test in its place.

The chat log corroborates the driver's account in his counterparty_statement — that this was the closure diversion and not a route of his own choosing — and it corroborates it from the rider's side. At 18:22:40 the driver wrote that the Pelton Canal Link closure was sending traffic around the industrial loop; at 18:23:10 the rider replied 'Understood, please take the lawful diversion.' The timing puts the rider's words before the vehicle left the optimal corridor, since the diversion-entry gantry is not charged until 18:29. The driver does not claim full exoneration under POL-RD-04: chat_message.waypoint_hint is null and the rider named no road, so the clause's corroboration test cannot be run on this record and, on POL-RD-04's own terms, the case is decided on the remaining clauses.

ruling.explanation: Both of you agree on the underlying facts, so this comes down to arithmetic. The GPS trace and the trip record agree the completed ride was 18.0 km against a booked optimal of 10.0 km — an excess of 8.0 km. The LTA advisory (ADV-20260920-113, Pelton Canal Link eastbound connector, closure 18:14–18:55) is a real event that overlaps the whole trip, and it does excuse part of that excess — but only part. Under POL-RD-03 the justified excess is capped at the lesser of the measured 8.0 km or 1.30 × (12.0 km shortest lawful alternative − 10.0 km booked optimal) + 1.0 km tolerance = 3.6 km. So 3.6 km is excused and 4.4 km is not. Driver: your closure argument succeeds for 3.6 km and fails for the rest. Rider: accepting the closure in chat is not a waiver of the excess the closure did not require, and the remaining 4.4 km is above the POL-RD-01 threshold measured against the adjusted route, so it stands as an unexcused deviation. The refund is then arithmetic under POL-RD-02 against the closure-adjusted optimal (13.6 km, 27.2 min, since the trip record stores no amended duration). The surge multiplier of 1.00 is read from the fare breakdown, the only artifact that carries it. Recomputed fare = (3.80 + 0.75×13.6 + 0.28×27.2) × 1.00 + 0.80 platform fee + 1.00 on-route ERP = 23.416. Charged total 31.42 − 23.416 = 8.004, rounded up to 8.05. That is 25.6% of the charged total, so it is a partial refund rather than a full one. On ERP: the 2.80 'Industrial loop exit' gantry is off the optimal route, and it is already comprehended inside this refund because the recomputed fare ignores it — under POL-RD-09(1) it is itemised for transparency but must not be added on top, and we have not done so. On the driver's second argument, that the rider asked for the detour: the rider's only chat message names no road or place and carries no waypoint hint, so POL-RD-04's corroboration test cannot be run and the clause is unavailable; this case is decided on the remaining clauses. On the driver's profile: the pre-adjustment deviation was material, so the POL-RD-06 check was run, and it is clean — deviation_flags_90d is 0 against 610 completed 90-day trips, so no repeat pattern is established, meaning no full-refund uplift and no conduct referral. On the trace: it is clean (205 fixes, 10-second interval, 100% coverage, no gaps), so it is not impaired for policy purposes and nothing escalates. The rider's initial burden under POL-RD-08 is discharged (one trip ID across the records, a qualifying excess), and the rider's 60-day claim counters are zero, so no extra corroboration was required. No escalation trigger fires and no clause produces a referral.
